Schedule SE deep-dive on private deployment architecture (Maya + Liam) week of 2025-04-28
Legal to review and request Redwood DPA + sample contract redlines (Priya)
Provide short benchmark (latency/cost) for hosting in EU vs Dedicated in US-east by 2025-04-30
Share example audit-logging export and SIEM integration notes (Splunk example)

header:
Date: 2025-04-23
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE); Maya Patel (Redwood SE); Sofia Martinez (Oceanshore, CISO); Liam O'Connor (Oceanshore, Head of Platform); Priya Das (Oceanshore, Legal); Noah Reed (Oceanshore, ML)
summary: Discovery focused on residency and compliance constraints for an LLM-powered assistant in wealth management. Primary topics: GDPR residency in EU/UK, HIPAA scoping for health-related client notes in narrow workflow, audit logging limits (retention & PII redaction), private/VPC vs Dedicated tradeoffs, and contract/DPA expectations. Customer asked for concrete evidence of data flows, SIEM hooks, and a Private deployment architecture that keeps customer data inside their VPC with key control.
transcript:
00:00 - Avery (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intro — Avery Chen on AE and Maya Patel, our solutions engineer. *little cough* we'll run through high level and then dive into the residency/compliance questions.
00:12 - Sofia (Oceanshore): Thanks. Sofia here, CISO. We run regulated wealth mgmt for high-net individuals across EU and US, so GDPR is the big one. Also want to understand HIPAA implications — we do sometimes get health info in client notes.
00:25 - Liam (Oceanshore): Liam here — platform. Our infra is multi-region in cloud, but finance wants EU-only for certain products.
00:34 - Maya (Redwood SE): Great. Quick agenda: how data moves in Redwood Hosted, what Dedicated gives you, and what Private/VPC looks like, plus audit/logging, KMS, and DPA items. We'll flag anything that needs legal follow-up.
00:48 - Priya (Legal): Quick note — we'll need to see a DPA and sample security appendix. Also curious about subprocessor list.
00:55 - Maya (Redwood): Totally. We'll share the full security package and subprocessor registry. For data residency: hosted API by default processes in region selected — we can pin EU region, but hosted is a multi-tenant control plane so certain metadata may cross boundaries.
01:14 - Sofia: Can you clarify "metadata"? e.g., logs, request IDs, traces — could those leave EU? That's a hard no for our EU clients.
01:22 - Avery: Good question. Short answer: request payloads and model context can be kept in-region if you pick EU-hosting; however platform-level operational logs (traces, some agent telemetry) may be routed to central control plane in US unless you’re on Private.
01:36 - Noah (Oceanshore): That's the crux. We need cert that PII from prompts never leaves EU. Is that possible with Hosted?
01:42 - Maya: Hosted can be configured to store and process data in EU region for production traffic; still, Hosted uses a Redwood-managed control plane. For guaranteed zero-egress of any PII, Private or Dedicated with VPC peering is stronger because you control network egress.
02:01 - (inaudible/mis-transcribe) Speaker 1: ... K-B cache, K-V cash caching ...
02:10 - Avery: Sorry, that was Maya referencing KV cache behavior. Key-value cache is per-instance and can be kept inside the region. I saw a note in your RFP about prefix caching and retention — we can disable or set TTLs.
02:22 - Priya: HIPAA — do you sign BAAs? What's Redwood's stance?
02:29 - Maya: Redwood can support HIPAA-covered workloads under a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments. Hosted is more nuanced — we can do it for certain enterprise accounts after legal review, but many customers prefer Dedicated/Private for HIPAA since you get isolation and contract terms more easily.
02:45 - Sofia: Our main concern is logging. Compliance requires audit logs for 7 years for certain products. What granularity do logs have, and can we redact PII from logs?
02:56 - Maya: Logs are configurable. We can scrub or mask prompt text at ingestion, store only metadata (request ID, model, latency, token counts). For full audit trails, we can provide encrypted logs to your SIEM via S3 export or syslog; and for Private deployments logs never leave your VPC unless you push them.
03:18 - Liam: SIEM integration — we use Splunk. Do you support forwarders or direct streaming?
03:24 - Avery: We have a Splunk HEC endpoint integration pattern and recommended transforms. We'll share a short example config.
03:30 - (background cross-talk)
03:36 - Sofia: Regarding encryption — do you offer customer-managed keys (CMK) / HSM? We must ensure keys are not held by vendor for certain data types.
03:44 - Maya: Yes. Private supports KMS integration and customer-managed keys. Dedicated also supports CMKs with some constraints. On Hosted, you can use Redwood-managed keys or bring-your-own-key for certain enterprise plans, but for strict key custody, Private is the cleanest.
04:02 - Noah: How is ephemeral KV cache treated for GDPR right-to-be-forgotten requests? If a client asks to erase their data, how quickly do caches drop?
04:11 - Maya: We have TTL controls; we can purge caches on-demand in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, we honor erasure requests and we have deletion flows, but absolute timelines depend on retention and backups. We can include guaranteed deletion SLA in contract for dedicated/private.
04:28 - Priya: We need a sample clause for data residency and deletion in the DPA.
04:34 - Avery: We'll include contract language and suggested redlines.
04:38 - (30s pause while link shared)
04:45 - Avery: I'm going to show a top-level flow — (mentions shared doc: security-package.pdf and private-arch.png).
05:00 - Maya: Diagram: for Private we deploy a control plane that you host in your VPC or we deploy a private control plane where no telemetry leaves. Model inference runs on instances in your VPC and KV caches are localized. We can provide Egress rules to block external traffic.
05:22 - Liam: Sounds good. What's the lift and how long to stand up a Private environment?
05:28 - Maya: Typical timeline 6-8 weeks for on-prem/self-managed private; shorter if cloud VPC with automation (2-4 weeks) depending on capacity and legal checks. Dedicated spin-up is faster — we provision reserved capacity in 2-3 weeks.
05:45 - Sofia: Costs — high level: what's the delta between Hosted EU and Dedicated?
05:50 - Avery: Hosted is pay-as-you-go. Dedicated is reserved monthly commit — more predictable but higher baseline. For EU residency the cost delta depends on required throughput, encryption, and logging retention; we'll generate a bench to show unit token costs.
06:08 - Noah: We also need to talk about model fallback and graceful degradation. If our EU cluster is saturated what happens? Could requests route to US fallback? That's a compliance risk.
06:18 - Maya: Policy-based routing — you can block cross-region fallback. We can set canary and fallback rules; for strict residency you can disable cross-region fallback and have queuing or throttling instead.
06:30 - (brief keyboard sounds)
06:35 - Priya: On sub-processors: do you use cloud AI accelerators that may be in other regions? For example, do kernels or compiled artifacts ever run in different regions?
06:44 - Maya: Compiled kernels are image artifacts; we ensure images are pulled into the region you specify. We can provide SBOM-ish info and an immutable artifact registry. We'll include a subprocessor list with regions.
07:00 - Sofia: Data exposure: our compliance team wants to know about debug dumps and how often full request payloads appear in logs for debugging.
07:08 - Maya: Debug dumps are off by default in production. If enabled, they're accessible only with elevated privileges and we can restrict them to Private deployments. We can set logging levels per environment.
07:25 - Avery: Few real-world notes — some banks have accepted Hosted for non-PII inference and Dedicated for PII workflows. Others went full Private when legal required full control.
07:37 - Sofia: Hmm. We will likely want a hybrid: Hosted for public/non-sensitive features, Dedicated or Private for client notes and sensitive workflows. Does Redwood support splitting routing by route or API key?
07:47 - Maya: Yes — routing is per API key / route. You can pin routes to specific deployments, models, and regions.
07:55 - Liam: About audit retention: we need immutability and export for e-discovery. Can you give us an example retention configuration?
08:03 - Maya: Example: store audit logs encrypted in S3 with object lock enabled for retention; daily export to your SIEM; 7-year retention policy as you need. We'll send sample retention configs.
08:16 - Sofia: Legal will want encryption attestations and SOC2 type reports and timeline of last penetration test.
08:22 - Avery: We'll include latest SOC2 report, pen test summary, and timeline for upcoming certs.
08:28 - (brief pause)
08:35 - Noah: On HIPAA — we have a narrow use case: advisors sometimes enter health info from clients re: suitability. If we store that in the assistant context, it may be PHI. Does Redwood provide PHI detection/redaction?
08:48 - Maya: We have PII/PHI detection libraries and can provide server-side redaction or client-side pre-processing. For PHI workflows we recommend Dedicated/Private and a BAA.
08:59 - Priya: How does encryption-at-rest work? Are keys segmented per customer?
09:05 - Maya: Yes — customer-specific keys are supported on Private and Dedicated (BYOK/KMS). Hosted can be configured for BYOK at enterprise tier, but not for all plans.
09:16 - Avery: Quick transcription hiccup — sometimes our scoring doc calls KNS instead of KMS in auto text — sorry, transcription quirks.
09:24 - (laughter)
09:28 - Sofia: One more: data subject access requests — we need to verify how Redwood surfaces logs per request or allows bulk export for legal hold.
09:38 - Maya: You can run exports by query (time range + API key) and we can also implement an API for data extracts to satisfy DSARs. For Private deploys that's a customer-managed job; for Hosted we’ll do it under contract.
09:52 - Liam: Performance: can you provide latency numbers for EU-hosted inference vs Dedicated EU cluster? We need p50/p95 for short prompts and long prompts.
09:59 - Avery: We'll run a short benchmark and share p50/p95 and cost-per-token for both. We'll also show the effect of prefix caching on latency.
10:12 - Priya: Legal: sample DPA please. Also will need to see evidence of data deletion — e.g., deletion logs or API.
10:20 - Avery: We'll include deletion audit examples and sample API calls to purge caches/logs.
10:26 - (background rustle)
10:30 - Sofia: How about backup copies? Snapshots — do they include raw prompt text? What is the backup retention?
10:37 - Maya: Snapshots depend on configuration. We can advise encryption and point-in-time recovery, and can configure backups to exclude prompt bodies or encrypt them under separate keys.
10:49 - Noah: For our PoC, we may feed synthetic but realistic prompts. Any guardrails on model outputs leaking earlier prompt content? I'm worried about cross-customer leakage.
10:58 - Maya: Our runtime isolates model context per request; we do not share KV cache across customers. We also run QA for model behaviors and provide model-variant pinning.
11:11 - Sofia: Ok. Let's recap next steps — and please make the DPA and subprocessor list high priority.
11:18 - Avery: Recap: 1) Send SOC2, HIPAA scoping and DPA template; 2) SE deep-dive on Private architecture; 3) Benchmark EU-hosted vs Dedicated; 4) Sample SIEM integration and log export; 5) Legal redlines exchange.
11:33 - Priya: We'll prepare our compliance checklist and share high-level contract must-haves.
11:39 - Avery: Great. Anything else?
11:42 - Liam: One tiny thing — can you show a minimal network diagram with ports and egress rules? That will help security review.
11:49 - Maya: Will do. We'll attach a simple VPC peering diagram and required ports.
11:54 - (muted goodbyes, small cross talk)
11:58 - Avery: Thanks all, we'll follow up within 24 hours with the package.
12:03 - Sofia: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-heard acronyms (KMS -> KNS, KV cache -> K-B cache). Shared artifacts: security-package.pdf, private-arch.png, sample-dpa.docx.
